# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially

## Context

AC5 requires PRD M3 to note competitive mode as a deliberate scope extension beyond M3 with rendering deferred to a planning-created child. AC6/AC7 require dedicated competitive tests, affected doc/comment updates, and build + full-suite verification. Competitive tests are per producer decision “dedicated” — one new file per sibling (not co-located).

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the shared street rendered with owner-coloured slots, shared-market phase alternation, and SFX/animations (per AGENTS.md §8), so competitive ownership is visually and audibly unambiguous.

## Context

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. This planning-created child (per AC5 “deferred to a planning child” and producer Q2 “planning”) captures the deferred rendering scope for the next milestone. Worker must use core-engine animation helpers with `soundManager` + `sfx` (AGENTS.md §8: every animated action needs sound + animation; SFX keys via `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, no literals).

## Scope

- Competitive scene (Phaser scene) with SLL layout.
- Owner-coloured street: each placed business's street slot tinted by owner (e.g. player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is immediately readable.
- Shared-market phase alternation: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day with visible whose-turn affordance.
- SFX/animations for all competitive actions (deal/flip/place/discard/illegal) via helpers + `SoundManager`, respecting reduced-motion and mute.
- Turn alternation SFX/animation sequencing so AI actions are visible (delayed AI turn like Coloretto precedent).

## Out of scope

- Engine state/phase/income/AI/Monte Carlo (parent epic siblings).
- Game-selector entry — include only when the scene is ready for play (within this child).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Competitive scene renders the shared street with per-slot owner colour (player vs AI unambiguously distinct); SLL layout used (no hardcoded pixel positions).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared-market phase alternation is visible (whose turn) and input is gated to the active player; AI turn is animated with a brief delay.
- [ ] **AC3:** Every competitive action that uses a core-engine animation helper is wired with SFX (via helper `soundManager`/`sfx` params or `GameEventEmitter`/`SoundManager`); SFX keys follow `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention; reduced-motion and mute respected.
- [ ] **AC4:** Build + unit tests pass; smoke browser coverage for the scene.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScene.ts` — Competitive scene (owner-coloured street, phase alternation, SFX).
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveRenderer.ts` — Owner-colour helpers (tinting by ownerId).
- `src/core-engine/SoundManager.ts` — `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` source of truth for SFX keys.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-scene.browser.test.ts` — Smoke/browser coverage.

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode (engine-only; rendering deferred here per AC5)
- Siblings: state, phase, income/events, AI strategy, Monte Carlo (engine foundation this child renders)
- AGENTS.md §8 — Every action with animation must have SFX

# Rename the re-roll button to 'Research'

## Problem Statement

The market has a "re-roll" action (button, tooltip, HUD tooltip, help text, in-game messages and activity log) that uses inconsistent, mechanical terminology. This item renames all user-facing "re-roll" / "Refresh Market" strings to the game's "Research" terminology, starting with the market button, while preserving cost visibility and all functional detail.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — "As a player, I want the market action to be called 'Research' everywhere it appears, so that the UI terminology is clear and consistent."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Button label:** The market button text changes from `Re-roll (${refreshCost})` to `Research (${refreshCost})`; the dynamic cost stays visible on the button face.
2. **AC2 — Button tooltip:** The hover tooltip headline is "Invest in researching new opportunities", followed by the existing functional detail (cost, card replacement, Market-phase-only availability, and the disabled reason when inapplicable), with "re-roll" wording changed to "research".
3. **AC3 — Consistent user-facing terminology:** All other user-facing "re-roll" / "Refresh Market" strings are renamed to "Research" terminology:
   - turn-controller instruction messages and activity log (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`),
   - the legality/disabled reason and the market-refresh activity log message (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`),
   - the help-panel "Tools" line (`src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`),
   - the HUD action tooltip line (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`).
4. **AC4 — No regressions:** The button and action remain fully functional (callback, disabled state, click behaviour, undo/redo, save/load) with no behavioural changes; only strings change.
5. **AC5 — Tests:** Affected tests are updated (notably `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts`, which asserts the help body contains 'refresh market'), and the new button label/tooltip wording is covered so the rename cannot silently regress.
6. **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (notably `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, which lists "Market re-roll/refresh").
7. **AC7 — Quality gate:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only user-facing strings, supporting code comments, tests and docs change. No game logic, balance, or data changes.
- The button cost stays visible (`Research (${refreshCost})`) — confirmed by the producer.
- The tooltip keeps the existing functional body and gains the new headline — confirmed by the producer.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — button label `Re-roll (${refreshCost})` (~line 168); tooltip `Pay €${refreshCost} to re-roll the market and replace all visible cards. Removed cards go to their discard piles. Available only during Market phase.${reasonSuffix}` (~line 184); comments mention "Re-roll button" (~lines 146, 148, 158, 182).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — instruction messages `Cannot re-roll: ...` (~287), `Re-rolling the market...` (~293), `Market re-rolled` (~305) and log `Re-rolled market (via UI)` (~306).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — legality reason `Re-rolling the market is only allowed during MarketPhase.` (~45) and activity log `Re-rolled market (-€${cost}): ...` (~110).
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help panel line `Refresh Market: re-roll the market row for coins (5, less with the Accountant).` (~138).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip `No action: re-roll market, sell, end turn. ...` (~118).
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — asserts the help body contains 'refresh market' (line 160); must be updated.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — "Free operations" list contains "Market re-roll/refresh" (~line 277).
- No other test asserts the exact user-facing re-roll strings (checked `refresh-market.test.ts`, `activity-log.test.ts`, `market-extraction-parity.test.ts`).
- The `createActionButton` helper returns a Phaser Container; the label is a `Text` child.

## Desired change

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`: label → `Research (${refreshCost})`; tooltip → `Invest in researching new opportunities.

Pay €${refreshCost} to research the market and replace all visible cards. Removed cards go to their discard piles. Available only during Market phase.${reasonSuffix}`; update the "Re-roll" comments to "Research".
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`: `Cannot re-roll:` → `Cannot research:`; `Re-rolling the market...` → `Researching the market...`; `Market re-rolled` → `Market researched`; `Re-rolled market (via UI)` → `Researched market (via UI)`.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`: legality reason → `Researching the market is only allowed during MarketPhase.`; log → `Researched market (-€${cost}): ...`; update comments.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts`: → `Research: research the market row for coins (5, less with the Accountant).`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts`: → `No action: research market, sell, end turn. ...`
- Update `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` and any other assertions on the changed strings; add coverage for the button label/tooltip headline (prefer a focused test; if a Phaser render test is brittle, use the repo's static source-guard pattern).
- Update `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — button label, tooltip and comments.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — instruction and log strings.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — legality reason, activity log and comments.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — help-panel "Tools" line.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — HUD tooltip string.
- `tests/main-street/help-panel-content.test.ts` — update the 'refresh market' assertion.
- `tests/main-street/market-research-button.test.ts` (new, or an existing market-renderer test) — cover label/tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — "Market re-roll/refresh" wording.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Confirmed (Q1):** cost stays visible as `Research (<cost>)` on the button face (producer: "visible").
- **Confirmed (Q2):** the new sentence is the tooltip headline and the existing functional body is retained (producer: "as recommended").
- **Confirmed (Q3):** all user-facing "re-roll"/"Refresh Market" strings are renamed (producer: "everywhere").
- **Risk (related item conflict):** `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` ("Reroll to cost more", plan_complete) AC4 requires the button label/tooltip to report the current escalated cost; keeping the cost in the label preserves that. Coordinate if both land.
- **Risk (test brittleness):** asserting Phaser GameObject internals can be brittle; prefer a static source guard if a render test proves unstable.
- **Risk (missed strings):** "everywhere" could miss a string; mitigation — grep the repo for `re-roll|reroll|Refresh Market` (case-insensitive) at implementation time and after the change.

## Related Work

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open, plan_complete): touches the same button label/tooltip and requires cost visibility; coordinate.
- `CG-0MTKMN7KG006F5EE` — "The cost of a reroll is still 5, it should be 500" (completed): set the flat base cost shown in this label.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): refresh-cost discounts shown in the label/tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions and Answers

- **Q:** What should the button label be, and should the cost stay visible on the face of the button?
  - Options: (a) `Research (5)` keep the cost; (b) `Research` cost only in tooltip; (c) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — preserves cost visibility and keeps `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` AC4 satisfiable.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "visible" — option (a) accepted; the cost stays on the button face.
- **Q:** How should the new tooltip text "Invest in researching new opportunities" relate to the existing detailed tooltip?
  - Options: (a) headline plus existing functional detail; (b) replace tooltip entirely with the sentence; (c) sentence plus phase/disabled reason only; (d) other.
  - **Recommended:** (a) — preserves actionable information.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-09-30):** "as recommended" — option (a) accepted.
- **Q:** Should the rename extend to other user-facing "re-roll"/"Refresh Market" strings, or only the button and its tooltip?

# Reduce time upcoming event is shown

## Problem statement

During the end-of-turn routine an incident card from the Upcoming queue is revealed at board centre and held face-up for 4 seconds (`4000ms`). That hold is longer than needed: once the coin/reputation delta bubbles have finished animating, the extra wait only delays the turn. The hold should be shortened to **1 second longer than the delta-bubble animation** (target ≈ 1920ms).

## Users

- **Main Street player**: Needs the incident card shown long enough to read it and see the coin/reputation delta bubbles land, but not so long that the end-of-turn routine drags. Example user story: *As a player, I want the Upcoming incident reveal to finish shortly after its coin/reputation bubbles land, so the next turn starts promptly without me losing the ability to read the incident.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Shortened hold (full motion)**: `animateIncidentReveal` holds the face-up incident card for `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` = **1920ms** — i.e. 1 second longer than the 920ms delta-bubble animation (600ms flight + 4 × 80ms max stagger) — replacing the previous 4000ms.
2. **Reduced motion parity**: the reduced-motion path uses the same `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` value; no duplicate hardcoded duration remains.
3. **No hang / exactly-once completion**: the `onComplete` callback still fires exactly once after the shortened hold + return animation, and the turn-advance chain is never left pending.
4. **Bubbles complete before the hold ends**: the delta-bubble animation window (max 5 bubbles × 80ms stagger + 600ms flight = 920ms) finishes before the hold elapses, so bubbles are never cut off.
5. **Single named constant**: the duration is defined once in `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` as a named constant, with the bubble flight/stagger values it derives from; no literal `4000` remains for the reveal hold.
6. **Testing/validation**: unit tests assert the new hold duration and the constant relationship (`hold = flights + stagger × (maxBubbles − 1) + 1000`); the incident-reveal browser test's timing expectations are updated to the shortened choreography.
7. **Documentation updated**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full suite green**: the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Turn-advance chain preserved**: the shortened hold must still fire `onComplete` exactly once; the turn must never hang or double-advance.
- **Bubble readability**: the new hold must not truncate the delta-bubble animation (target 1920ms > 920ms bubble window).
- **Reduced-motion preserved**: reduced-motion players must still get a readable hold (no flight/flip/bubbles, but the hold remains) — per the original design (CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I).
- **Replay/headless unchanged**: replay mode remains a no-op that still fires `onComplete`.
- **No incident**: when no incident resolves, the animation stays a complete no-op (no delay added).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` → `animateIncidentReveal()` contains the hold as a hardcoded `4000` in two places:
  - the reduced-motion path (`s.time.delayedCall(4000, () => { cleanup(); })`), and
  - the full-motion path (after the hinge flip: `s.time.delayedCall(4000, () => { … return animation … })`).
- `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles()` launches up to 5 bubbles per resource at `i * 80ms` with a `600ms` flight — a 920ms window — using local `flightMs = 600` and literal `80` staggers.
- Nominal full choreography today: flight 550ms + hinge 260ms + hold 4000ms + return 400ms ≈ 5210ms.
- The reveal blocks the day start until the hold completes (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.finishTurnPresentation`).

## Desired change

1. Introduce a named hold constant (e.g. `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`) in `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`, derived from the bubble animation: 600ms flight + 4 × 80ms stagger + 1000ms buffer = **1920ms**. Extract the bubble flight/stagger literals into named constants so the relationship is explicit and the hold cannot silently drift shorter than the bubble window.
2. Replace both hardcoded `4000` hold delays in `animateIncidentReveal()` with the new constant (full-motion and reduced-motion paths share it).
3. Update the incident-reveal unit and browser tests to the shortened choreography (including the "4000ms hold" assertions and timing-margin comments).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — replace the two hardcoded `4000` hold delays in `animateIncidentReveal()`; extract the `600`/`80` bubble literals in `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles()` into named constants.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — add `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` (≈1920ms) plus `INCIDENT_BUBBLE_FLIGHT_MS` (600) and `INCIDENT_BUBBLE_STAGGER_MS` (80), with a derivation comment.
- `tests/main-street/incident-reveal-animator.test.ts` — update the `delay >= 4000` hold assertions to the new constant; add an assertion tying the hold to the bubble window.
- `tests/main-street/incident-reveal.browser.test.ts` — update the choreography timing notes/margins to the shortened hold.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Upcoming card reveal in end-of-turn routine*: introduced the 4-second hold and bubble choreography this item shortens; its "timing is fixed: 4 seconds" constraint is deliberately superseded here.
- **CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end-of-turn cycle*: owns the deferred-mutation / deferred HUD window that the reveal's `pendingDeltas` participates in.
- **CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS** (in_review, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Reputation and coins from Upcoming should flow in the correct direction*: owns Upcoming delta routing (attached vs HUD) and the coin/reputation flights referenced by this item.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Income Phase: phased card-effect animations*: the phased income choreography that runs before the reveal.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption** — "the animation for the coins and reputation" means the delta-bubble animation during the reveal hold (600ms flight + up to 4 × 80ms stagger = 920ms), confirmed by the operator. Target hold = 920ms + 1000ms = **1920ms**.
- **Assumption** — the reduced-motion path keeps the same 1920ms hold (rather than being shortened to ~1000ms with no bubbles), preserving readable time per the original design. Revisit with the producer only if a shorter reduced-motion hold is wanted.
- **Risk** — if the bubble count or stagger changes later, a hardcoded 1920ms could truncate the animation; mitigated by deriving the constant from the bubble flight/stagger constants.
- **Risk** — timing-based tests are brittle; the unit test should assert against the constant (not a magic number) where practical, and browser tests keep generous margins.
- **Risk** — shortening the hold interacts with the deferred HUD window and the incident-reveal → day-start chain; the exactly-once `onComplete` guarantee must be preserved.
- **Scope-creep risk** — requests to change the flight/hinge/return durations or add new reveal effects are out of scope and must be raised as separate work items.

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q1**: The description says "Reduce this to 1 second longer than the animation for the coins and reputation". Which animation is the reference point?
  - Options presented: (1) the delta-bubble animation during the incident hold (~920ms = 600ms flight + 4 × 80ms max stagger) → target ≈ 1920ms; (2) the coin flight duration (`INCOME_FLIGHT_MS` = 600ms) → target ≈ 1600ms.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive): Option 1** — the delta-bubble animation time, target hold ≈ 1920ms.
  - Evidence: `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` (`animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`, `flightMs = 600`, stagger `i * 80`).
- **Q2** (resolved by repo inspection, no operator input needed): Where is the hold implemented and how long is it? — `animateIncidentReveal()` hardcodes `4000` in both the full-motion and reduced-motion paths. Source: code inspection.

- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: animation, coins, end, event, longer (+9 more)
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: animation, coins, end, event, longer (+8 more)
